answer: ASIC-resistant randomized-program minting resists sybils: each mint executes a pseudo-randomly GENERATED program (RandomX-style) so no fixed circuit can be optimized, keeping general CPUs competitive and denying bulk-hardware economies. A crystal rig of specialized chips gains little when every mint runs a different instruction mix; the ridge of cost stays near commodity-CPU level per identity. A saffron-dusted farm minting thousands pays near-CPU cost for each, so aggregate expense scales linearly with head count instead of collapsing onto cheap specialized silicon.
